 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal No.508 Of 2024

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. This appeal is filed by the State aggrieved by the order of acquittal by the learned Sessions Judge.
The respondent/accused was prosecuted for the offences under Sections 417, 420 and 376 of IPC.

2. Heard learned Assistant Public Prosecutor on behalf of the State and the learned counsel appearing for the respondent/accused.
3.
The case of the prosecution is that the de-facto complainant/P.W.1 lodged a complaint on 22.12.2015 alleging that she was in love with respondent/accused for 5 years who is a close relative.
She went to movies and other places believing that the accused would marry her.
During the said period, they were also in sexual relation.
P.W.1 along with her parents went to the house of accused and requested him and his parents to perform the marriage, however, the proposal was denied and they were sent back.
Aggrieved by the said denial to marry, the complaint was filed.
4. The Police having investigated the case filed charge sheet for the alleged offences.
5. The learned trial Judged examined P.Ws.1 to 6 and marked Exs.P.1 to P.13.
Learned Sessions Judge found that accused was not guilty for the said offences mainly on the ground that nowhere in the complaint, it was stated that there was any kind of force that was used.
Even according to her and her own statement, she had sexual intercourse with the appellant and went to movies and other places on her own for around 5 years.
6. P.W.1 is major and admits that the accused was a relative and she moved closely, went to movies and other places on account of their love affair.
They were also in sexual relation over the said period.
The only reason for lodging the complaint is that the accused refused to marry P.W.1.

Mere refusal to marry will not amount to an offence of cheating unless it is proved by the prosecution or evident from the circumstances that there was any kind of inducement or mis-statement made deliberately to have physical or sexual relation.
In the present complaint, when P.W.1 admits that she was having love affair, went along with the appellant on her own, the question of cheating or committing rape on P.W.1 does not arise.
There are no grounds to interfere with the findings of the learned Sessions Judge.
7. The State appeal fails.
Accordingly, the Criminal is dismissed.
